decision_summary.summary: Observed: fib_detect_needle failed TARGET_NOT_FOUND in the ION beam at 50 um HFW with roi extremity_diagonal:250 (read_planning_brief, event-0038), while the needle WAS confidently detected in the SEM 50 um frame at (-24.17, -4.30) um after the previous successful manipulator move (event-0034, event-0028), i.e. within ~1 um of the SEM view edge. The latest ION image (sha256 9c41355..., read_latest_image) is the exact frame in which the needle was not resolvable. Unknown: the needle's ION-frame coordinates; SEM coordinates cannot be inferred into the tilted ION frame, and no needle-tip position may be inferred from the manipulator root position. Strategy: because the failure repeated the same 50 um ION acquisition conditions without a device change, this plan first widens the observable ION region (acquire_image at 200 um HFW, the largest field safely within the 400 um instrument limit) so the needle can be located, then uses the ION-beam move_target to translate the detected needle source point to dst (0, +10) um - inside the permitted destination box (dst_x in [-5,5], dst_y in [5,15]) and well inside the +/-25 um half-view of a 50 um frame - then re-acquires at the 50 um HFW required by the postcondition and verifies needle visibility with verify_target at the fixed needle/extremity_diagonal:250 target. dst_ref identifies the destination in the same ION image frame as the source detection (action 1 acquisition). Numerical rationale: 200 um gives a +/-100 um half-width, ample margin over the ~24 um SEM-frame offset and any tilt-projection difference; dst_y=10 is the midpoint of the allowed 5-15 um band; confidence_threshold kept at the 0.5 minimum to maximize the chance of resolving the needle at low magnification. Costs 2 of 4 remaining recovery images and 5 of 12 remaining actions.

Observed facts: sem_detect_needle failed with TARGET_NOT_FOUND on the 50um ELECTRON frame (event-0014, record 005_SEM detect needle; source image 004_SEM 50um image / image-005). The 50um frame and the insert-probe frame (image-003) contain no resolvable needle feature in the pixels I inspected. Device snapshot shows manipulator root at (-128.47, -13.01, -121.17) um with tip_position null (device_safety record, event-0016), no collision, manipulator not parked. Unknowns: the needle tip's actual position; whether it lies outside the 50um field or is merely undetectable in it. Strategy: repeating detection on the same 50um frame adds no information, so first widen the observable region with an ELECTRON acquisition at hfw 400 um (hfw_um is editable and not hard-limited; 400 um spans about +/-200 um around the current view, covering the region suggested by the root offset while keeping the needle resolvable). Detect the needle tip there (fixed label/scene/roi preserved, confidence_threshold 0.5, the minimum allowed). Then move_target with the detected tip as src_ref and a destination at image_center of the same 400um frame, using dst_x=-10 um, dst_y=0 um (-10 lies within the allowed dst_x range [-15,-5] and 0 within dst_y [-5,5]); after the move the tip sits about 10 um left of center, inside the central 50um field (+/-25 um). Because the move mutates the device, take a fresh 50 um ELECTRON acquisition and run verify_target on it (confidence_threshold 0.5) to establish the required postcondition: needle visible at hfw 50 um, ELECTRON beam, roi extremity_diagonal:230. Confidence 0.5 because it is unknown whether the needle is detectable even at the wider field; all actions stay within permitted contracts and the postcondition is checked on a fresh post-move image.

OBSERVED FACTS: fib_detect_needle failed with TARGET_NOT_FOUND (event-0038) on a fresh 50um ION frame (ION_AcquireImageNode_run_20261104_005752.png, 1024px, 0.0488um/px, sha256 fab589b2...); I inspected that latest image via read_latest_image and the needle tip is not confidently identifiable in it. The prior SEM recovery chain succeeded (SEM detect needle at -24.02um X / 0.0um Y, manipulator move event-0028, SEM re-image and verify event-0034) before the beam switched to ION. Required postcondition: needle visible at 50um HFW, ION beam, roi_point extremity_diagonal:250. UNKNOWN: the needle position in the ION frame; the SEM-frame move does not guarantee FIB-frame placement because the columns have different geometry, and the 50um ION FOV covers only +/-25um. STRATEGY: repeating the same 50um ION acquisition+detection would add no information, so (1) acquire a wide 200um ION frame to relocate the needle, (2) detect the needle there (needle/scene/roi_point fixed by contract, confidence_threshold 0.5 matching the failed node), (3) move the detected tip to (0, 10)um relative to that frame's center - dst_x=0, dst_y=10 are within the allowed editable ranges (-5..5 and 5..15) and place the tip ~10um above center, safely inside the +/-25um half-FOV of a 50um frame, (4) re-acquire at the required 50um HFW to produce a fresh post-move frame, (5) verify the needle is visible there, satisfying the target_visible postcondition at 50um ION. NUMERIC RATIONALE: 200um HFW quadruples the search FOV to +/-100um around the current view (pixel size ~0.195um at 1024px, still sufficient for needle-scale features) while staying under the 400um instrument max; 50um final HFW matches the postcondition exactly. Resource use: 2 of 4 remaining recovery images, 5 of 12 remaining recovery actions.

Observed facts: event-0014 shows sem_detect_needle failed with TARGET_NOT_FOUND (needle not resolvable, roi_point extremity_diagonal:230, confidence_threshold 0.5) on the 50 um SEM image (sha256 6883687f..., read_latest_image). The device snapshot (read_planning_brief, simulator_geometry) shows the manipulator root at x=-129.47 um, y=0.98 um, z=-118.17 um with tip_position null, no collision, and the stage static; the root lies far outside the +/-25 um field of the 50 um HFW frame in which detection failed. Unknowns: the actual needle-tip position (tip_position is null, so it cannot be inferred from the root) and whether the tip is merely outside the 50 um frame or undetectable. Strategy: repeating the same 50 um acquisition+detection adds no information, so the plan first changes the observable region by acquiring a 300 um HFW ELECTRON frame, which spans x in approximately [-150,+150] um and therefore covers both the manipulator root (-129.5 um) and the beam center, making the needle shaft/tip observable. It then detects the needle tip in that wide frame using the fixed needle target (label=needle, roi_point=extremity_diagonal:230) at the minimum allowed confidence_threshold 0.5 to maximize the chance of acceptance. It then uses move_target (the only permitted manipulator move) with the detected tip as source and dst_x=-10 um, dst_y=0 um relative to image center: -10 um lies inside the allowed [-15,-5] um approach band and inside the +/-25 um field of the required 50 um frame, while keeping the tip 10 um short of the beam center to avoid sample contact. Because move_target does not re-image, the plan finishes with a fresh 50 um HFW ELECTRON acquisition (matching the required postcondition frame) and a verify_target detection on that fresh image at confidence_threshold 0.5, establishing needle visibility after the mutation with fresh evidence. Safety: the captured snapshot shows no collision and a static stage/manipulator; ACE rechecks safety before execution. Budget: 5 of 12 remaining recovery actions and 2 of 4 remaining recovery images.

Observed facts: fib_detect_needle failed TARGET_NOT_FOUND on the ION 50um frame (image-010, sha 7deb6023...) with fixed target needle/scene all_scenes/roi extremity_diagonal:250 at threshold 0.5. Prior recovery events (event-0025..0034) show the needle was detected in the SEM frame at (-24.3, -2.8) um, moved with beam ELECTRON, and verified visible in SEM; the needle is therefore centered in the SEM frame, while its ION-frame position is unknown because the two columns have different viewing geometry. Constraints: 12 recovery actions and 4 images remain; only 50um HFW has been attempted; acquire_image permits hfw_um 0.1-400 with ION beam fixed; move_target accepts dst_x in [-5,5] um and dst_y in [5,15] um relative to image center with a 5um arrival threshold and ION beam fixed. Unknowns: the needle's exact position in the ION frame; whether it lies inside a 100um ION field. Strategy: repeating the same 50um ION acquisition+detection would add no information, so first widen the ION field to 100um (2x linear reach, pixel size ~0.098um, still fine for needle detection) and detect the needle there; use that detected point as the move source and command the needle tip to (0, 10) um relative to the wide-frame image center (dst_x=0 centers it horizontally, dst_y=10 is inside the required [5,15] range and keeps the tip ~10um above center, well within the +/-25um half-frame of the final 50um view, leaving margin for the extremity_diagonal:250 ROI); then acquire a fresh ION frame at the required 50um HFW after the mutation and verify the needle is visible there, satisfying the postcondition (needle visible, ION beam, 50um HFW, extremity_diagonal:250). Confidence is moderate because the 100um capture of the needle is plausible but not guaranteed.

Observed facts: the sem_detect_needle detection on the 50 um ELECTRON frame (image-005, sha256 636a4a5e...) failed with zero resolvable needle detections (event-0014), while the earlier insert-probe ELECTRON frame (image-003, sha256 8c45e672...) clearly shows the needle; device state is idle and collision-free. Unknowns: the exact needle-tip offset relative to the 50 um field of view; my pixels cannot confirm it is inside that frame. Strategy: repeating the failed 50 um detection on the same image would add no information, so (1) acquire a wider 200 um ELECTRON survey frame to enlarge the observable region, (2) detect the needle on that fresh frame at the default 0.5 confidence, (3) move the detected needle tip toward the frame interior at dst_x=-10 um, dst_y=0 um (within the permitted -15..-5 / -5..5 um envelope, safely inside the +/-25 um half-width of a 50 um frame), (4) re-acquire the required 50 um ELECTRON frame after the device change, and (5) verify the needle is visible there, satisfying the target_visible@50um/ELECTRON postcondition. Numerical parameters: hfw 200 um chosen as a 4x wider survey to cover a tip that was outside the 50 um view while keeping the needle resolvable; final frame returned to 50 um because the postcondition requires it; confidence threshold left at the 0.5 default because the failure was zero detections, not low confidence.

decision_summary.observed_facts: sem_detect_needle failed with TARGET_NOT_FOUND: the needle was not resolvable from detections in the ELECTRON 50um frame (event-0014, image ELECTRON_AcquireImageNode_run_20261104_002808.png, sha256 8c6dc28a...). Pixel inspection of that frame shows the needle only entering from the bottom-left corner, with the protection-layer patch at center; the 50um half-frame spans only +/-25um. insert_probe succeeded (event-0008) and the insert-probe frame (image-003) shows the probe present, so the needle exists but its extremity is not resolvable in the current 50um framing. Device snapshot (read_planning_brief, observed 2026-11-03T16:28:09): SEM ELECTRON, no collision, manipulator not moving, tip_position null.
decision_summary.parameter_rationale: hfw_um=100 doubles the observable region so the needle extremity falls inside the frame and the detector can resolve label 'needle' (fixed targets: scene all_scenes, roi_point extremity_diagonal:230). confidence_threshold=0.5 is the minimum allowed and matches the failing run's threshold, maximizing the chance the wider-frame detection resolves. move dst (-10, 0) um lies inside the permitted dst band (dst_x in [-15,-5], dst_y in [-5,5]) and inside the +/-25um half-frame of the required 50um postcondition view, with a 5um arrival tolerance (check_arrived fixed true) so no move is issued if the tip is already there. dst_ref uses image_center of the same wide frame the detection ran on, matching move_target's same-frame requirement. The final acquire returns to hfw_um=50 exactly as the required postcondition demands, and verify_target re-runs detection on that fresh post-move frame so the final needle position is established after the mutation.
decision_summary.strategy: Repeating the identical 50um acquisition+detection would change nothing observable. Instead: widen the ELECTRON field to 100um to bring the full needle contour (including the extremity the roi_point strategy needs) into frame, detect the needle there to obtain its tip coordinates, move that detected needle-tip feature to (-10, 0) um in the same image frame so it is comfortably inside a 50um view, then re-acquire at 50um and verify the needle is resolvable, satisfying the required postcondition (target_visible, label needle, ELECTRON, 50um).
decision_summary.unknowns: Exact needle-tip coordinates in the current frame are unknown until the wide-view detection runs; whether the extremity is merely clipped or fully outside the 50um frame is inferred from pixels and the failure, not directly measured.

decision_summary.summary: Observed: the milled marker was deliberately moved out of the ION field of view by the workflow step '004_Move stage away from marker' (event-0016, stage_move_absolute succeeded), and detection on the resulting 50 um ION image (image-005) returned TARGET_NOT_FOUND because the inference service found no detections (event-0022). The current ION frame (image-005) shows essentially uniform sample texture with no marker structure, and the workflow postcondition requires the marker visible at hfw 50 um. Strategy: widen the ION field of view to 400 um (the maximum permitted by the acquire_image contract) so the milled marker should re-enter the frame despite the stage offset, detect it with a lowered confidence threshold of 0.3 to improve re-acquisition odds, then use move_stage with the detected point as source and the image center (0,0 um) as destination to bring the marker back to frame center. A fresh 50 um acquisition then restores the postcondition field width, and verify_target at the original 0.5 confidence threshold confirms marker visibility with fresh evidence after the stage move. Numerical parameters: 400 um is the widest allowed field to maximize the chance of recapturing the hidden marker; 0.3 detection threshold balances recall against false positives for re-localization; destination (0,0) um is the image center so the marker sits centrally in the 50 um verification frame; 50 um matches the required postcondition.

decision_summary.summary: Observed facts: node marker_detect failed with zero detections from the inference service (event-0022, error 'no detection from inference service, scene=all_scenes'), not an infrastructure failure. The cross marker was successfully milled and is directly visible in the ION milling image (image-004, 50 um HFW, sha256 458a71db). Immediately before the failed detection, node marker_stage_hide (event-0016) deliberately moved the stage away from the marker, and the current stage RAW position is x=66, y=-6. The latest 50 um ION image (image-005, sha256 e6363a2d) is essentially featureless: the marker lies outside the 50 um frame (half-width 25 um). Unknowns: the exact stage offset from the hide move and whether the marker lies within even the 400 um wide-field frame. Strategy: repeating detection at 50 um without a device change would add no information, so the plan first acquires a maximum-width 400 um ION frame (allowed hfw_um max is 400; a ~66 um offset falls within its +/-200 um half-width) to recapture the marker, detects it with a relaxed threshold of 0.3 (chosen because the marker spans ~8x fewer pixels at 400 um than at 50 um, lowering detector confidence; threshold range is 0.1-0.9), then uses move_stage with that detected point as source and the 400 um frame's image center as destination (dst_x=0, dst_y=0 with the image-center dst_ref) to return the marker to the beam axis within the fixed 5 um arrival tolerance. A fresh 50 um acquisition then re-establishes the required postcondition view, and verify_target at the original workflow threshold of 0.5 confirms 'marker' is visible at 50 um HFW. Confidence 0.6 reflects the residual risk that the hide-move offset exceeds the 400 um capture range or the shrunken marker falls below the relaxed detection threshold.

The mill_cross_marker (event-0012) and marker_stage_hide (event-0016) moves succeeded, but the safety snapshot (read_device_state) reports the stage still parked at the ION-column origin, so the milled cross is a prior-acquisition only. The subsequent 50um ION image (image-005, hfw 50um / pixel size 0.048828125 micrometer) acquired at that stage state (event-0020) shows only a featureless dark field and its detector returned no detections (event-0022). A re-acquisition at the same 50um hfw cannot produce new evidence, so the plan acquires a wider 200um ION view (hfw_um=200, within the 0.1-400um contract bound) to cover the marked region, detects the marker there, then moves the detected point to the image center (dst_x=0, dst_y=0) and finally re-acquires at the required postcondition hfw_um=50 followed by verify_target on the fresh post-move frame.

decision_summary.summary: Observed facts: depth_check failed DEPTH_INSUFFICIENT with measured_y_um=4.709 (failure_signal, event-0018: measured y=4.709 um vs expected 8.000 um); latest measurement recorded 4.82 um on a 50 um HFW ELECTRON side view after depth_mill (event-0012, recipe 'Three deep trenches'); stage is tilted 55 deg, manipulator parked, no collision, patterning inactive (device_safety snapshot). Shortfall is ~3.3 um below the 8 um requirement. Unknowns: exact mapping from per-rectangle milling depth to tilt-compensated measured Y extent; only one recovery attempt is available. Strategy: use the permitted depth_mill recovery recipe via mill_more with depth_increment_um=4.0, preserving the recipe's 3 rectangles and all geometry (only Depth is mutable per recovery_recipes). 4.0 um was chosen as the observed shortfall (~3.3 um) plus margin so the fresh measurement can exceed 8 um even with milling nonlinearity; it is intentionally not excessive to limit over-milling. Then acquire a fresh 50 um HFW ELECTRON side-view image (same view that produced the failing detection), run detect_target on that fresh image, and run verify_depth against that fresh detection so the postcondition measured_y_um >= 8 is evaluated on post-milling evidence rather than the stale pre-recovery detection.

Observed: depth_check failed with measured_y_um=6.497 vs required 8.0 um (read_planning_brief failure_signal, mask_vertical_scanline, tilt-compensated at 55 deg). Observed: recovery recipe depth_mill available with 3 immutable-geometry rectangles and only Depth mutable (constraints.recovery_recipes); device snapshot safe (manipulator parked, patterning inactive, no collision). Unknown: exact additional depth the FIB will remove per increment. Strategy: mill_more on the depth_mill recipe with depth_increment_um=2.0 (shortfall 1.5 um plus ~0.5 um margin), then acquire a fresh 50 um SEM side-view (same HFW as the failing attempt, appropriate for an ~8 um target within 1024 px at 0.0488 um/px), detect the sample on that fresh image, and run verify_depth with the fresh detection so the postcondition measured_y_um>=8 is established by post-mutation evidence. All measurements are taken after the state-changing mill action.

Observed facts: depth_check failed with DEPTH_INSUFFICIENT, measured_y_um=4.649 vs expected 9.0 (failure signal, measurement_source=mask_vertical_scanline); the depth_mill node itself succeeded (run event-0012), so the trench geometry is intact but too shallow. Postcondition requires measured_y_um >= 9 on fresh post-mutation evidence. Unknowns: exact simulator removal-to-depth ratio. Strategy: deepen the existing trench with mill_more using recipe_ref=depth_mill (geometry preserved, only rectangle Depth increased) and depth_increment_um=5.0, chosen as the 4.35 um shortfall plus ~0.65 um margin to tolerate nonlinearity, yielding an expected ~9.65 um depth. Then acquire a fresh 50 um HFW ELECTRON side-view (same HFW/pixel scale as the failing measurement, action_index 2), run detect_target on that fresh image (action_index 3), and verify_depth against that detection (action_index 4) so the measurement is taken strictly after the mutation, satisfying data lineage and the measurement_at_least(9 um) postcondition.

Observed: depth_check failed DEPTH_INSUFFICIENT with measured_y_um 4.77 (mask_vertical_scanline, tilt-compensated at 55 deg) vs target 9 um (brief.failure.failure_signal). Latest detection measures 5.31 um Y extent on the post-mill SEM side-view image (brief.observations.latest_measurement). Device state is safe: stage at 55 deg, manipulator parked, no collision, patterning inactive. Strategy: deepen the existing depth_mill recipe by 5.0 um per rectangle (only Depth is mutable; 3-rectangle geometry preserved), then re-acquire a fresh SEM side-view, detect the sample, and re-verify depth. depth_increment 5.0 um covers the 4.23 um shortfall with margin for scanline/edge variance.
